Bacterial_spot.pathogen: Xanthomonas spp. (tomato, pepper); Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni (peach)
Bacterial_spot.symptoms: Small, water-soaked, dark brown-black leaf spots, often with a yellow halo; spots may merge and leaves drop.
Bacterial_spot.fertilizer: Balanced NPK 19-19-19 at label rate; avoid excess nitrogen, which produces soft, susceptible growth. Add calcium (calcium nitrate) to strengthen tissue.
Bacterial_spot.pesticide: Copper-based bactericide (copper hydroxide or copper oxychloride), optionally tank-mixed with mancozeb. Rotate products and follow the label and local regulations.
Bacterial_spot.precautions: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants; avoid overhead irrigation and working in wet foliage; remove infected debris; rotate crops for 2-3 years.
Bacterial_spot.severity_hint: Spreads fast in warm, wet weather (24-30 C).

Black_rot.symptoms: Purple-bordered 'frog-eye' leaf spots on apple; tan-brown circular lesions with dark margins on grape leaves; fruit rot and mummies.
Black_rot.fertilizer: Potassium-rich fertiliser (e.g. sulphate of potash) to improve tissue strength; keep nitrogen moderate.
Black_rot.pesticide: Protectant fungicides such as captan or mancozeb; myclobutanil for curative action. Follow the label and local regulations.
Black_rot.precautions: Prune out cankers and dead wood; remove mummified fruit; improve airflow by pruning; destroy fallen leaves.
Black_rot.severity_hint: Infection risk peaks during warm, rainy periods in spring.

Healthy.symptoms: Uniform green colour, no lesions detected.
Healthy.fertilizer: Continue the normal nutrient schedule based on a soil test (e.g. NPK 20-20-20 foliar feed every 2-3 weeks during active growth).
Healthy.precautions: Keep monitoring weekly; maintain good field hygiene, balanced irrigation and crop rotation.

Late_Blight.symptoms: Large, greasy, grey-green to brown lesions, often with white sporulation on the underside in humid conditions; rapid collapse of foliage.
Late_Blight.fertilizer: Avoid excess nitrogen; apply potassium and phosphorus (e.g. NPK 10-26-26) to support tuber and fruit development.
Late_Blight.pesticide: Systemic plus contact fungicides such as metalaxyl-M + mancozeb, cymoxanil + mancozeb, or chlorothalonil. Follow the label and local regulations.
Late_Blight.precautions: Destroy infected plants and volunteer potatoes; use resistant varieties; ensure good drainage and spacing; avoid evening irrigation.
Late_Blight.severity_hint: Can destroy a field within 1-2 weeks in cool (10-25 C), humid weather. Act immediately.

Powder_Mildew.pathogen: Podosphaera spp. (cherry, squash) and other Erysiphales
Powder_Mildew.symptoms: White to grey powdery fungal growth on leaf surfaces; leaves may yellow, curl and dry.
Powder_Mildew.fertilizer: Avoid excessive nitrogen; use balanced NPK with adequate potassium. Foliar potassium bicarbonate also suppresses mildew.
Powder_Mildew.pesticide: Wettable sulphur, potassium bicarbonate, or systemic fungicides such as hexaconazole or myclobutanil. Follow the label and local regulations.
Powder_Mildew.precautions: Improve air circulation and sunlight; remove heavily infected leaves; avoid dense planting; water at the base of plants.
Powder_Mildew.severity_hint: Favoured by dry leaves with high humidity and moderate temperatures (20-27 C).
